1.explanation:
All of these functions in lib/rules/key-spacing.js participate in determining and enforcing colon/value alignment on object literals:

• initOptionProperty and initOptions parse the rule configuration (including the align: "value" setting) and propagate it to the rest of the rule logic. Because "value" alignment is enabled unconditionally, every object literal is treated as a candidate for vertical alignment—even inline JSX style objects.

• isSingleLine tests whether a node spans a single line or not. When it returns false for a multi-line literal (e.g. broken across soft wraps in JSX), the rule enters the multi-line alignment path.

• groupProperties takes a list of object literal properties and splits them into contiguous groups for alignment.

• verifyVerticalAlignment is the core routine that, for each property group, calculates the target column for every value and then inserts or removes padding so that all values line up vertically. It is this logic that reformats the style object inside JSX.

To prevent JSX-embedded objects from being mangled, these functions need to be adjusted so that multi-line alignment is skipped (or handled differently) when the object literal appears inside a JSXExpressionContainer (i.e. in a style prop).
1.bug_scenario: When ESLint’s key-spacing rule is configured with { multiLine: { align: "value" } }, any object literal—even those inside JSX props such as style={{…}}—is treated as a multi-line group and gets re-aligned on fix. In the screenshots you can see that a compact style object in a JSX attribute is broken apart and its properties forcibly re-aligned, which mangles the intended formatting inside the JSX curly braces.

2.explanation: All of the listed functions live in the key-spacing rule implementation and participate in parsing the configuration (initOptions and initOptionProperty) and enforcing spacing and alignment on object literal properties (verifyProperties, verifySpacing, verifyVerticalAlignment). The create(context) function is where the rule hooks into the AST and invokes those checks on every ObjectExpression – including those in JSX attributes. Because none of these functions currently distinguish between plain JavaScript object literals and inline JSX style objects, the rule applies its multiLine.align behavior inside JSX and produces the misaligned output. To fix the bug, the logic in create (or early in verify*) should detect when an ObjectExpression is a child of a JSXExpressionContainer/JSXAttribute and skip the multiLine alignment code for those cases.
2.bug_scenario: When running ESLint with the key-spacing rule configured for multiLine.align: "value", object literals inside JSX attributes (e.g. style={{ marginRight: '4px', color: '#0C090A', … }}) get reformatted across multiple lines and then realigned in an ugly way. The rule treats the small inline style object in JSX just like any other object literal, splitting properties onto separate lines and aligning the values, which is not desired inside JSX expressions.
